label: A long letter
prompt:
Please summarise this letter from my energy supplier in plain English, and tell me exactly what I need to do and by when.

---

Dear Customer,

Account number: 0000 0000 0000
Supply address: 1 Example Street, Exeter

IMPORTANT INFORMATION ABOUT CHANGES TO YOUR TARIFF AND ACCOUNT

We are writing to inform you that your current fixed-rate tariff is scheduled to end on 30 September. In accordance with the terms and conditions of your supply agreement and our obligations under the relevant regulatory framework, we are required to give you advance notice of the changes that will take effect from that date.

Following the conclusion of your fixed term, and in the absence of any alternative instruction from yourself, your supply will transfer automatically onto our standard variable tariff. Under this arrangement, the unit rate applicable to your electricity supply will increase from 22.4p per kilowatt hour to 27.9p per kilowatt hour, and the daily standing charge will increase from 48.2p to 61.5p. For your gas supply, the unit rate will increase from 5.9p per kilowatt hour to 7.1p per kilowatt hour, with the daily standing charge rising from 29.1p to 32.4p. Based on your consumption over the preceding twelve-month period, we estimate that these revised rates would result in an increase to your annual expenditure of approximately £294.

We would like to draw your attention to the fact that alternative tariffs are available. Our twelve-month fixed tariff offers a fixed unit rate of 24.1p per kilowatt hour for electricity and 6.2p per kilowatt hour for gas, with a daily standing charge of 52.0p and 30.2p respectively. Should you wish to move onto this tariff, you may do so without incurring an exit fee at any point prior to the conclusion of your existing fixed term. Please note that an early exit fee of £35 per fuel would ordinarily apply to that tariff should you choose to leave it before the end of its term, although this fee is waived within the final forty-nine days of the term.

In addition, our records indicate that we have not received an actual meter reading from your property since 11 March. The bills issued to you since that date have therefore been produced on an estimated basis. We would be grateful if you could provide an up-to-date reading, as this will ensure that your account is accurately reconciled prior to the tariff change taking effect. Readings can be submitted through your online account, via our automated telephone service, or by returning the enclosed card.

We are also required to remind you that you have the right to switch to an alternative supplier at any time, and that a comparison of available tariffs can be obtained from any accredited price comparison service.

If we do not hear from you before 30 September, no action will be taken on your part and the changes described above will proceed automatically.

Yours sincerely,

Customer Accounts Team

label: A cover letter
prompt:
Here is a job advert and my background. Please write me a tailored cover letter of around 350 words, in British English, that draws directly on my experience and addresses the specific requirements listed.

--- JOB ADVERT ---

Community Engagement Officer
A community library service in Exeter
Salary: £29,400 – £32,100 depending on experience
Contract: Permanent, full time (37 hours per week, including occasional evenings and Saturdays)

About the role

Our library service runs eleven community libraries and two mobile library services across the Exeter area. We are looking for a Community Engagement Officer to lead our programme of public events, outreach and partnership work, ensuring that our libraries are genuinely welcoming and useful to everybody in the communities we serve.

You will be responsible for designing and delivering a year-round programme of activities for a wide range of audiences, from under-fives storytelling sessions through to digital skills workshops for older residents. You will work closely with branch managers, volunteers, local schools, and voluntary sector partners, and you will play a central role in helping us reach people who do not currently use our services.

Key responsibilities

- Design, deliver and evaluate a varied programme of public events and activities across all eleven branches
- Build and maintain partnerships with schools, community groups, health services and voluntary organisations
- Recruit, train and support a team of approximately forty volunteers
- Manage an annual programme budget of around £48,000, ensuring value for money and accurate reporting
- Collect and analyse participation data, and produce quarterly reports for our board
- Support funding applications by providing evidence of impact and community need
- Represent the library service at local partnership meetings and public events

Essential criteria

- Demonstrable experience of planning and delivering community events or public programmes
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to adapt your approach for different audiences
- Experience of working with volunteers
- Confidence in handling budgets and producing clear written reports
- A genuine commitment to widening access and reducing barriers to participation
- Willingness to work occasional evenings and weekends

Desirable criteria

- Experience of working in libraries, museums, heritage or the wider cultural sector
- Experience of contributing to grant applications or fundraising
- Knowledge of the Exeter area and its communities
- Experience of working with data and evaluation frameworks

--- MY BACKGROUND ---

I am currently a Volunteer Coordinator at a local food bank, where I have worked for three years. I recruit and support around sixty volunteers across four distribution centres, and I run the induction and safeguarding training for all of them. Before that I spent two years as an Events Assistant at a small independent theatre in Exeter, where I helped run a schools outreach programme and a monthly community open day.

I have managed a small budget of about £12,000 a year for volunteer expenses and training, and I produce a monthly report for our trustees covering volunteer numbers, retention and hours contributed. Last year I helped write a successful £25,000 grant application to a national community fund, mainly by pulling together the participation data and case studies.

I grew up in Exeter and still live there. I do not have direct library experience, but I have worked with several of the same community partners, including two local primary schools. I have a degree in History.
